That the armies of the greatest powers have known for ten years the harmfulness of depleted uranium munitions, even for those who use them, proves only that the general staffs show their own soldiers the same disregard as they do for the civilian population and the enemy forces.

Since the beginning of the atomic age with World War II, the dangers and precautions associated with handling uranium and other radioactive materials have been well known, as it is a highly toxic (chemically and radiologically toxic) element if inhaled or absorbed, and it is also genetically dangerous.

The use of this type of weapon by the United States and other NATO countries during the Gulf War, in Bosnia and Kosovo has already caused the death of many soldiers, suffering and fatalities among the inhabitants of the bombed areas and the contamination of the environment in the affected regions.

Given the scale of crimes against entire civilian populations, it is urgently necessary to identify the main perpetrators of these criminal acts against humanity, establish their guilt and condemn them, and to immediately prohibit the manufacture, testing, use, and sale of weapons with depleted uranium, and not just to accept a moratorium.

We all know that these weapons, which were used by NATO in the Gulf War (1991), in Bosnia (1994-95) and in Kosovo (1999), had serious consequences first for the bombed civilian population, but also for the environment and the military personnel of NATO, the Iraqi, Bosnian, Serbian and Kosovar armed forces.

Mr. President, after all the tragic events in connection with the bombing of Yugoslavia and the revelations about the use of depleted uranium munitions, it is now urgently necessary to ban this type of weapon, which even after its use continues to have dangerous effects for a long time and indiscriminately, i.e. without any recognizable distinction, affects all those who are at risk of coming into contact with it.

Equally important and urgent is the development of a comprehensive policy of aid, prevention, and remediation for all the areas in Yugoslavia that are suffering the consequences of the use of these munitions, in order to protect public health and the environment, remediate soils and water, and ensure sustainable economic development of the country and the entire region.

Apart from that, while the resolution proposal briefly touches upon extremely serious issues concerning the analysis and necessary research of depleted uranium, it fails to address the ongoing efforts to conceal facts, independent research known to us all, and even scientific publications from NATO countries that prove the danger of depleted uranium and outline the precautionary measures these countries impose on their armed forces.
